mira: heads up — hitting a weird interaction between token refresh + our paginator that causes duplicate page fetches under heavy load. Repro included in sampleapp. Steps: start sampleapp with prefetch=3, blast with a client burst. Random 401 triggers token refresh in middleware, the retry path reuses the stale page cursor and we fetch the same page twice which spikes token usage -> host returns 429. Logs:
```
[fetch] page_token=abc123
[auth] 401 -> refresh
[retry] fetch page_token=abc123
[api] 429 rate_limit exceeded
```
Minimal repro gist: https://gist.github.com/redwood/mira-paginate-repro
Snippet from sampleapp (JS):
```js
for await (const page of client.paginate({resource: 'items'})) {
  // process page
}
```
Observed only in JS SDK (v1.6.3) — py-sdk appears to await refresh before next() so it doesn't duplicate. Any ideas?
jason: can you paste the sampleapp config and exact sdk version? pinging @sven in case it's a middleware ordering bug.
mira: sdk: 1.6.3, sampleapp config: prefetch=3, concurrency=4, retry=enabled (default backoff). Repro happens when auth refresh race dovetails with prefetch window; retry middleware replays the fetch with the original cursor before the refreshed token is applied to the inflight fetch promise.
devx-bot: rate-limit-bot: detected spike -> 429s (service=api, window=1m, count=112) :warning:
sven: probable root cause: token-refresh race + prefetch. Two quick mitigations: 1) serialize refresh so any inflight paginate operation that hits 401 awaits the same refresh promise instead of re-issuing with stale headers; 2) attach a per-page idempotency key based on the page cursor so retries that replay the same cursor are deduped server-side. Pseudo-fix on client side:
```js
// naive lock
if (token.isExpired()) await refreshLock.wait();
// or
await refreshLock.acquire();
try { if (isExpired(token)) await refresh(); } finally { refreshLock.release(); }
```
Also consider adding a small backoff/jitter before retrying a paginated page when a 401 was observed to allow token propagation.
alejandra: file a bug in SDK repo (label: sdk-js, backpressure, auth). Add an integration test that returns a 401 on one of the prefetch pages mid-iteration. Also check parity with go-sdk and make sure behavior is documented in the onboarding troubleshooting guide.
mira: will open PR with serialized-refresh + test. I'll also add an optional flag `paginator.awaitAuthOnPrefetch` default false so we can enable on high-risk onboarding flows. Will note in release notes that this fixes duplicate page fetches and reduces burst 429s. CC @ryan.
ryan: thanks — when PR lands please add a short blurb to onboarding docs: "If you see 429s during first-run/onboarding, reduce prefetch or upgrade to SDK >= 1.6.4. Also include a sampleapp config snippet showing `prefetch: 1` or `awaitAuthOnPrefetch: true`."
